approachQuestion.prompt:
Schedule by deadline with bounded labels

Each job has an integer deadline in [0,U]. Return every job ordered by nondecreasing deadline; jobs with equal deadlines may appear in either order. The input may be reordered.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; 1 ≤ U ≤ n; each deadline is an integer in [0,U]. U is supplied with the input.

Examples: n=3, U=3, jobs=[(a,3),(b,1),(c,3)] → [(b,1),(a,3),(c,3)] or [(b,1),(c,3),(a,3)]. n=2, U=2, jobs=[(X,2),(Y,1)] → [(Y,1),(X,2)].

Choose a valid method that meets the full contract with the least unnecessary work.
constraints: Each deadline is an integer in [0,U].
Return every job; jobs with equal deadlines may appear in either order.

options.text: Use comparison merge sort by deadline.
options.feedback: Correct for all inputs, but the stated bounded integer domain permits a method whose work depends on n+U and is asymptotically better when U is small.

options.text: Count jobs at each deadline, then traverse deadline values in order and emit that many jobs from corresponding buckets.
options.feedback: A frequency array orders the bounded keys directly; storing job records in buckets preserves all jobs.

options.text: Return only the number of jobs at each deadline.
options.feedback: The contract requests every job in order, not a frequency summary.

feedback.reason: The bounded deadline universe permits direct bucket indexing.
details: Allocate U+1 buckets, append each job to its deadline bucket, then concatenate buckets from 0 through U.

The bounded deadline universe permits direct bucket indexing. Visiting deadlines in ascending order orders every job without comparison sorting. Bucket allocation and traversal still cost work even for empty deadline slots.
“Use comparison merge sort by deadline.”: Correct for all inputs, but the stated bounded integer domain permits a method whose work depends on n+U and is asymptotically better when U is small.

“Count jobs at each deadline, then traverse deadline values in order and emit that many jobs from corresponding buckets.”: A frequency array orders the bounded keys directly; storing job records in buckets preserves all jobs.
“Sort by deadline descending.”: The requested order is nondecreasing.
“Return only the number of jobs at each deadline.”: The contract requests every job in order, not a frequency summary.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed revealed method, n is the number of jobs and U is the largest allowed deadline; the input guarantees 1 ≤ U ≤ n. Count bucket initialization, traversal and storage, and count the returned sequence as output space excluded from auxiliary space. The bucket array stores n job references; bucket concatenation writes the already-counted output. Choose the tightest worst-case bounds.

options.text: O(n + U) time, O(n + U) additional space
O(n log n) time, O(n) additional space
O(n + U) time, O(1) additional space

feedback.reason: Count n job insertions and U+1 bucket positions.
details: Initializing and traversing U+1 buckets and inserting each of n jobs takes O(n+U) time. The bucket array stores n references and has U+1 slots, so auxiliary space is O(n+U); because U≤n, these are both O(n). Comparison sorting is valid but slower in this bounded domain. Quadratic time overstates the work, while constant space omits the required buckets.
